openThreads: NOTHING RECORDS THE SERVED COMMIT TODAY, on either product. This is the row's central finding and the next action is a deploy change, not a code change: the Cloud Run deploy must pass SERVED_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) (or set the commit-sha revision label) and the Vercel console deploy must be made from a clean tree so meta.gitCommitSha is an identity. Until then the check refuses on both live surfaces and the row's predicate cannot be enforced, only measured as UNMEASURED.
The check is DORMANT: no deploy hook and no schedule. Wiring it is the single highest-value follow-up and it requires credentials in the deploy path, which is planner-owned territory.

meta.gitDirty: 8 of 10 smart-files production deployments, including the one serving today, were built from a dirty tree, so the console's recorded commit is an upper bound. The remedy is deploying the console from a clean checkout; until then a console-side 'dirty' should be read as a caveat on every parity verdict, which is why the check prints it on every run.

A tree-identical merge (main merging a branch that changes no file) reads as DISAGREE. Left strict on purpose; if the planner wants content-equality to count as agreement, the surface would need to report the tree hash as well, and that is a new rule rather than a bug fix.
Two smart-files production deployments record their commit only under meta.githubCommitSha; the reader accepts both, but any other tool reading only meta.gitCommitSha would refuse them.

The legacy deployments with no recorded commit cannot be backfilled: a deployment made without git context has no commit to recover. The three smart-files deployments that carry a SHA all have one; the two github-only ones do too.

The /version surface is unauthenticated, like GET /. It reports a commit SHA, which is public-repo information, and no data. If the planner wants it gated, that is a one-line change, but a gated version surface cannot be probed by a deploy-time hook without a credential in the deploy path.

LESSON: A deploy can be perfectly healthy and still be the defect. On 2026-09-17 plan-review's API answered every probe and the console answered every probe; what was missing was any surface on either side that could say WHICH COMMIT IT WAS SERVING. Every health check in the fleet passed. When a fact is not recorded anywhere, no probe can notice it -- so the instrument has to add the record, not just read harder.

A recorded commit is not necessarily the content served. Vercel records meta.gitDirty=1 when the tree had uncommitted changes: measured on smart-files 2026-09-18, 8 of 10 production deployments carry it, including the one serving. So meta.gitCommitSha is an upper bound, not an identity, and a parity check built on it is only as strong as the cleanliness of the deploy. Print the flag on every run; never let a reader assume the SHA is what shipped.

Two deploy paths record the same fact under two different field names: the Vercel CLI writes meta.gitCommitSha and a GitHub-integration deploy writes meta.githubCommitSha. A reader that knows one name will refuse a deployment that did record its commit -- 2 of smart-files' 10 production deployments are exactly that case. Read both; refuse when they disagree.

A merge commit and its branch tip can have the SAME TREE (smart-files 6d71bf3 over 1caeb98, `git diff --stat` empty). Commit-identity and content-identity are different predicates, and a strict check will report a disagreement where no user sees any difference. That is fail-loud, which is the right direction, but it has to be documented or the next reader will read it as a bug.

A git blob id is sha1('blob <len>\0' + content), so a Cloud Run source archive can be attributed to an exact commit without checking anything out -- IF line endings are normalised. A Windows archive compared raw against git's LF storage reads as 100% mismatch on a correct commit. Normalise to LF before hashing, or every candidate looks wrong.

`vercel ls --format=json` returns an OBJECT with a deployments array, not an array. And the dpl_ id another lane records does not appear as a usable join key in the CLI's JSON, so cross-lane matching must use the recorded commit and ref instead of the deployment id.

A lane must read its own instrument's output, not just its exit code. A reconstruction run printed a smart-files header over plan-review's revision and service while exiting correctly; no test would have caught it, and a reader could have concluded the recorded split was in the wrong product.

This wave's lane claims live in the SEAT worktree's doc_repo (P:/seat-worktrees/<seat>/doc_repo/_catalog/lane_claims.json), not in P:/doc_repo. The integration checkout's registry did not contain this lane while this lane was running it.
DEAD_END: Building the parity check on /healthz. GFE intercepts that exact path on *.run.app, so the probe measures the edge, not the process (both READMEs record this). /version was chosen for exactly this reason, and the live check confirmed the shape: the deployed smart-files revision answers 404 on /version while GET / answers 200.

Deriving the API's commit from the image tag, the revision tag, the deploy message or the revision creation time. On this fleet the tags name a LANE, not a commit (g155-search-reason, g150-reasoner), so every one of those is a proxy. The record does not exist today; the honest answer is to refuse and say the deploy must record it.

Assuming a Cloud Run revision records its own git revision. It does not: the revision carries no commit label, and the image is built from an uploaded source archive with .git excluded by .dockerignore, so the image cannot derive its commit either. Nothing about the source is recoverable except by fingerprinting the archive.

Trying to make the check accept a tree match so a no-op merge would pass. It weakens the row's own rule ('the same commit') to fix a nuisance, and the failure mode this row was carded from is a check that passed when it should have refused.

Looking for the Vercel deployment id as a cross-check key. The CLI's JSON did not expose the dpl_ id another lane recorded, so the join was abandoned in favour of the recorded commit + git ref, which is the actual subject.
